subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU options, TPS/concurrency, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU options, TPS/concurrency, next steps

Alex / Taylor — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps from today's discovery call so we can converge on a sizing recommendation for Dedicated capacity.

Recap (what we heard)
- Workload: real-time customer-facing chat + async batch embeddings for search.
- Current traffic: ~1,800 daily active users; peak traffic window ~2 hours/day.
- Target latency: p95 generation <= 300ms for S0 prompts (<=128 tokens).
- TPS target for peak: ~120 TPS sustained during peak hour (concurrent inference across routes).
- Token mix: ~40% short (<=64), 45% medium (64-512), 15% long (>512).
- Security: must stay inside VPC for production; initial proof-of-concept can use Dedicated with private networking.

Open sizing questions for you to confirm
1) Confirmed peak TPS: is 120 TPS the max sustained target or a burst target?
2) Concurrency: how many parallel sessions do you expect (approx.)? You mentioned 200 concurrent users in peak window — is that accurate?
3) Token distribution above is our interpretation — please flag if long-form usage is higher.
4) Any hard constraints on GPU type (e.g., prefer H100 family for throughput or A10G / A30 for cost)?

Next steps (recommended)
- I attached a first-pass proposal (acme-capacity-proposal-v1.pdf) and a spreadsheet with sizing options (redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx).
- Rafael and Aditya from our team are looped in to propose two sizing options (cost vs throughput) and a mini POC plan.
- Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to finalize counts and confirm procurement timeline?

Availability: I have Tue/Wed 10-12 PT next week.

Thanks — talk soon.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU options, TPS/concurrency, next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the deck/spreadsheet. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak TPS: 120 TPS is a sustained target during the 2-hour peak; we expect short spikes up to ~180 TPS for brief periods (a few minutes) during marketing-driven events.
- Concurrency: expected concurrent sessions ~220 during peak; many sessions are short-lived but spawn multiple calls (so effective concurrency for the model is higher).
- Token mix: the numbers you listed look right; note that a small subset (~5%) of events are long-form agents (>1k tokens) but they can be routed to a lower-priority queue.
- GPU preference: procurement will prefer cost-effective options but engineering has said H100 is preferable for our high-throughput routes; if there's a cost delta, we can look at mixed fleets.

We can do Tue 11am PT for the follow-up next week. Please include Rafael and any infra folks who will own the VPC setup.

Also copying procurement (procurement@acme.com) — they will want the sizing + SOW for budget approval.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU options, TPS/concurrency, next steps

Thanks Alex — good context. Rafael and Aditya, adding you explicitly to propose 2 practical sizing options below (we'll surface cost delta and POC approach):

Sizing options (first-pass)

Option A — Cost-conscious / mixed fleet (recommended for steady workloads with lower burst tolerance)
- GPUs: 4x NVIDIA A40/A10G-equivalent nodes (mixed instance pool)
- Estimated sustained TPS: ~100-140 (depending on batch size and KV caching)
- Concurrency: 8-12 per GPU instance (application-level concurrency) => ~150-200 effective concurrent streams across the pool
- Token mix: use customer-provided distribution (40/45/15) for cost calc; enable prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce token compute
- Notes: lower cost; may see higher tail latency on long-form requests unless offloaded to separate worker pool

Option B — Throughput-first / H100 pool (recommended for high-peak and bursty workloads)
- GPUs: 2-4x NVIDIA H100 nodes (model dependent; prefer H100 for high-batch throughput)
- Estimated sustained TPS: ~180-250 (with batching and larger KV cache tuning)
- Concurrency: 24-48 per GPU node => handles spikes to ~300 TPS for short bursts
- Token mix: optimized with dynamic batching thresholds; long-form (>1k) routed to lower-priority queue or smaller batch window to protect latency SLOs
- Notes: higher hourly cost but superior p95/p99 latency under burst, simpler routing to meet p95 <= 300ms for S0 prompts

POC recommendation
- 2-week pilot on Dedicated with one H100 node + 1 A10G node (mixed) to validate latency and cost tradeoffs using real traffic replay.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and tail latencies for long-form prompts.

Next steps
- Rafael / Aditya: can you confirm feasibility and add any infra-specific constraints (VPC peering, private gateway, KMS) and timing for POC?
- Alex / Taylor: confirm Tue 11am PT works and whether procurement wants a formal SOW or ballpark numbers first.

If you prefer, I can upload an updated spreadsheet with Option A/B side-by-side and an expected monthly cost range for each.
—
Marissa

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU options, TPS/concurrency, next steps

Alex / team — quick engineering note from my side after reviewing Marissa's options and the spreadsheet: 

1) H100 pool (Option B) is the safest way to meet your p95 <= 300ms requirement under bursty traffic. For the mix you described, I'd recommend starting with 2x H100 nodes for the initial POC and a horizontal autoscaling plan that can add up to 4 nodes for extreme events.

2) Consider enabling token-aware routing + prefix KV caching for the top ~20% of repeated prompts — this can reduce effective token compute by ~20-30% and lower required GPU count.

3) Concurrency tuning: we should tune batch windows per route. For chat S0 routes, target ~12-16 concurrent in-flight requests per GPU for stable latency; for embedding/batch jobs separate worker fleet with lower-cost GPUs (A10G/A30).

4) Networking/KMS: we'll need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for production. Aditya, I'll defer to you on the exact checklist; procurement will need a short SOW listing these integration items.

Proposed next steps
- Run two-week POC: 2x H100 + 1x A10G for embeddings + traffic replay.
- Marissa: I'll prepare an internal short SOW and a POC runbook.
- Schedule Tue 11am PT sync to finalize.
\Happy to hop on the call — I can share the POC runbook before the meeting.
—
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
